raw_response:
I'm 62 this year, been farming these same fields in Quzhou for 50 years — started helping my father when I was 12. My wife and I have 25.1 mu, all in wheat-maize double cropping. Just the two of us now, and we're not getting any younger, so labor and cash are always on my mind.

The winter wheat I planted last October is already in the ground and looking alright. I sowed an improved variety — been using it for five or six years, does well here. Back in October I put down about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and I irrigated once in March when the wheat greened up. I topdressed with about 50 jin of urea per mu at jointing in late March — the extension guy always says 40 jin, but I add a bit more. Better to waste a little money than risk a bad year. Right now the wheat is at booting, and it's been dry, so I'll irrigate once more around heading in early May, and if the weather stays hot and dry I'll do one more at grain filling in late May. Three times total this season. I always spray fungicide once at heading — can't skip it. Lost nearly half my crop to head blight back in 2013, never again. I'm hoping for about 480 kg per mu, maybe a bit more if the late spring rain helps.

Come mid-June, as soon as the combine finishes the wheat, I've got maybe five or six days to get the maize in or I miss the window. At my age I can't run like I used to, so I hire two or three guys from the village to help, or I use the custom planter service — costs money, but we need the speed. I plant Zhengdan 958, hybrid seed. Everyone around here grows it, and the seed shop always has it. I put compound fertilizer in the planting furrow, about 80-100 jin per mu, then when the maize is knee-high I topdress with urea. For water, I'll irrigate once or twice — usually once when it's about six leaves tall, and if July and August are dry like last year, maybe a second time at tasseling. I'll spray herbicide right after planting, and keep an eye out for armyworm. Expecting around 520 kg per mu.

After maize harvest in late September, there's no rest — straight into preparing for next winter wheat. I plow under the maize stubble, spread base fertilizer, and plant by mid-October. Same as always. I know some of the younger farmers do no-till, but I've tilled my whole life and it works for me.

Money is tight. Seed, fertilizer, pesticide, and irrigation electricity for three crops on 25 mu will run me about 24,000 yuan this cycle. That's a lot of cash out the door. My wife and I do most of the scouting, irrigating, and spraying ourselves, but we hire labor for planting and harvest — our backs aren't what they used to be. I keep some cash in reserve. You never know when the pump breaks or someone gets sick.
